result.topic_en: Modular relations between the Rogers–Ramanujan continued fraction at x and at x^2, x^3, x^4, at -x, and between the fifth power and the fraction at x^5, numbered (10)–(14).
result.transcription:
(10) If $u = \sqrt[5]{U} = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\cdots$
and $v = \sqrt[5]{V} = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x^2}}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^4}{1+}\frac{x^6}{1+}\cdots$
then
(a). $\frac{v-u^2}{v+u^2} = uv^2$
(b) $UV^2(U^2+V) + U^2 - V + 10UV(UV-U+V+1) = 0$
(c) $U$ and $V$ are satisfied by the relation
when $t \le \sqrt{5}-2$, $U = t\cdot\left(\frac{1-t}{1+t}\right)^2$ and $V = t^2\cdot\frac{1+t}{1-t}$.
(11). If $u = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\cdots$ and
$v = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x^3}}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\frac{x^6}{1+}\frac{x^9}{1+}\cdots$
then $(v-u^3)(1+uv^3) = 3u^2v^2$.
(12) If $u = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\cdots$
and $v = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1-}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1-}\frac{x^3}{1+}\cdots$
then
$uv(u-v)^4 - u^2v^2(u-v)^2 + (1+u^5v^5)(u-v) + 2u^3v^3 = 0$
(13). If $u = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\cdots$ and $v = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x^4}}{1+}\frac{x^4}{1+}\frac{x^8}{1+}\cdots$
then,
$u^5v^5 + uv + (u^5+v^5)(uv-1) = 5u^2v^2(uv-1)^2$
(14) If $u = \frac{\sqrt[5]{x}}{1+}\frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^2}{1+}\frac{x^3}{1+}\cdots$ and $v = \frac{x}{1+}\frac{x^5}{1+}\frac{x^{10}}{1+}\frac{x^{15}}{1+}\cdots$
then $u^5 = v\cdot\frac{1-2v+4v^2-3v^3+v^4}{1+3v+4v^2+2v^3+v^4}$.
